Action Plan:
1. Acute worsening of asthma control:
   • Increase preventer (Clenil – beclomethasone) from 3 puffs to 4 puffs twice daily immediately.  
   • Continue reliever (Salbutamol “blue” inhaler) up to every 2 hours PRN; seek emergency care if this frequency is required or symptoms deteriorate.  
   • Book an urgent face-to-face GP appointment within the next few days for chest examination, peak-flow measurement and assessment of need for oral steroids and/or antibiotics.  
   • Attend Emergency Department (A&E) without delay if shortness of breath worsens before review.  

2. Overdue routine asthma review:
   • Arrange formal asthma review with practice nurse (last review 2 years ago) to reassess control, inhaler technique, triggers and provide an updated asthma action plan.  

Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: 2–3-day history of chest tightness, wheeze, dry cough and shortness of breath; began while running, now occurs with brisk walking.  
• Reliever (Salbutamol) gives minimal relief; using several times daily.  
• Preventer (Clenil/beclomethasone) currently 3 puffs BID; using daily.  
• No sputum production, fever, chest pain or hospital admissions.  
• Last asthma attack 3–4 years ago; no oral steroids previously.  
Past Medical History: Asthma; hay fever; possible eczema patches (self-reported).  
Medications:  
  – Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented), PRN.  
  – Clenil (beclomethasone) 3 puffs BID (will increase as above).  
  – Cetraben cream.  
  – Topical hydrocortisone (dose/freq not documented).  
Allergies: No known drug allergies; seasonal hay fever.  
Family History: Brother – asthma; sister – eczema.  
Social History: Physically active runner; smoking/alcohol not discussed.

Objective:
• No physical examination performed (video consult).  
• Patient-reported usual peak-flow ≈ 380 L/min; current value not measured.  
• No vitals or auscultatory findings available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute shortness of breath / wheeze  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Asthma exacerbation (High likelihood per DDx).  
   - Differential diagnosis:  
     • Viral URTI triggering asthma (Medium).  
     • Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction / poor inhaler technique (Medium).  
     • Pulmonary embolism (Low).  
     • Early community-acquired pneumonia (Low).  
   - Investigations planned: Peak-flow measurement and chest examination at face-to-face GP visit; further tests (e.g., spirometry, CXR) if findings suggest alternate pathology.  
   - Treatment planned: Increase Clenil to 4 puffs BID; Salbutamol up to every 2 hours PRN; consider oral steroids ± antibiotics after in-person assessment; emergency attendance if deterioration.  
   - Relevant referrals: None beyond urgent GP appointment; attend A&E if worsening.

2. Routine asthma control review  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Stable chronic asthma requiring scheduled review.  
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable.  
   - Investigations planned: Formal asthma review including peak-flow diary, inhaler technique check, trigger assessment.  
   - Treatment planned: Update long-term management plan based on review findings.  
   - Relevant referrals: Asthma nurse clinic.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: Smoking status, alcohol intake, occupation, current peak-flow, vitals, and documented inhaler technique not obtained.  
• Internal conflicts: None identified between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional minor audio gaps not affecting key clinical content.
